title: Regional Parks Botanic Garden

services.name: School Tours
services.desc: The Botanic Garden offers free, docent-led school tours. Here is a description of the types of tours offered. Schools can request any tour at least 4 weeks in advance by completing the School Tour Request Form. For schools in Oakland and West Contra Costa county school districts in which at least50 percent of the student population qualifies for the Federal School Lunch Program, bus transportation from the school to the Garden and back, paid for by the Friends of the Botanic Garden, is available for the California Native Peoples and Plants (CNPP) tour, which complements the Native American Studies Unit for 4th graders. services.name: Garden Tours
services.desc: The Friends of the Regional Parks Botanic Garden, a part of the Regional Parks Foundation, is an all volunteer-run organization dedicated to supporting the Garden's important work in education, horticulture, and conservation of California native plants. Since being founded in 1996, the Friends has provided funding for many important Garden projects including: the Crevice Garden, plant collection field trips, docent training, path building, and planting bed improvement. By becoming a member of the Friends, you contribute directly to preserving and enhancing the Garden for the benefit of all visitors and you enjoy the many benefits of membership, including discounts at native plant nurseries,

blurb: The Regional Parks Botanic Garden is a naturally beautiful and tranquil living museum of California native plants. Located within Tilden Regional Park in the hills above Berkeley, California, this enchanting 10-acre garden is a sanctuary for many of the state's rare and endangered plants and a place for visitors to wander among trees, shrubs, flowers, and grasses from plant communities throughout the state.
